title: West Africa Needs Its Own Draghi Moment
gist: Truncated commentary opening: Morra and Wiedenbrüg argue Senegal's debt crisis, triggered by the discovery of previously undisclosed liabilities, is being misdiagnosed by both the restructure-now and adjust-and-reform camps as a fiscal problem. Because West Africa's monetary union members cannot devalue the shared currency, the real constraint is earning foreign exchange — via internal adjustment or an export push — to repay external creditors.

insights.claim: The discovery of previously undisclosed liabilities revealed the true, larger size of Senegal's public debt and has reduced the country's political debate to a single question of whether to restructure.
insights.speaker: Fernando Morra
insights.so_what: Hidden-liability discovery is a recurring emerging-market credit event pattern; Senegal is the current live case for frontier debt holders.

insights.claim: Both sides of Senegal's debate — economists urging restructuring and those arguing fiscal adjustment plus stronger institutions can restore confidence without creditor losses — mistakenly assume the challenge is primarily fiscal.
insights.speaker: Fernando Morra
insights.so_what: If the constraint is foreign-exchange generation rather than the primary balance, fiscal-consolidation-only programs will fail and restructuring odds are higher than consensus implies.

themes.theme: Monetary Union as the Binding Constraint

insights.claim: Because members of West Africa's monetary union cannot devalue the shared currency, they must either endure painful internal adjustment or boost exports to earn the foreign currency needed to repay external creditors.
insights.speaker: Fernando Morra
insights.so_what: The absent devaluation channel makes West African sovereign credit behave more like eurozone periphery risk than typical frontier local-currency risk.

insights.claim: Senegal's debt crisis has exposed a deeper structural vulnerability inside West Africa's monetary union rather than being an isolated single-sovereign event, making it the union's biggest test to date.
insights.speaker: Fernando Morra
insights.so_what: Treat Senegal as the trigger for repricing the whole West African monetary union's sovereign complex, not as an idiosyncratic story.
insights.quote: Senegal’s debt crisis has exposed a deeper vulnerability within West Africa’s monetary union.
